mcpServer.title: Magi MCP server
mcpServer.desc: Expose Magi's file, search and change-ledger tools to other agents (Cursor, Claude Desktop, …) over standard MCP. Every write asks for your approval in Magi first, and changes land in a revertible ledger.
mcpServer.enableHint: Listens on the loopback address only and requires a token. Turning it off drops every connection immediately.
mcpServer.status.port: The port is fixed at {port} and survives restarts
mcpServer.token.empty: No tokens yet. Create one and put it in your MCP client's configuration.
mcpServer.token.profile.edit_trusted: Trusted edit: writes no longer ask, deletes still do
mcpServer.token.profile.exec: Edit and run commands: every command asks
mcpServer.token.confirmHighRisk: I understand the risk of this permission level
mcpServer.token.created: Token created. Copy it into your client configuration; you can always view it again with “View configuration”.
mcpServer.token.revokeAllConfirm: Revoking all tokens immediately invalidates every configured client. Continue?
mcpServer.snippets.hint: The token in the configuration comes from the Clients tab: each MCP client has its own token, and you can view it again at any time with “View configuration” on its card. Pick a client below and its token is filled into the configuration; copy and paste it into that client.
mcpServer.snippets.stdio: stdio (local clients; the command is Magi's built-in mcp-relay)
mcpServer.snippets.needStart: Enable the server to see configuration.
mcpServer.tray.title: An external client needs approval
mcpServer.audit.clearAllConfirm: Clear all {count} call records? Only the review log is removed; tokens, approvals and the change ledger are not affected.
mcpServer.audit.clearClientConfirm: Clear the {count} call records of "{client}"? Only the review log is removed; tokens, approvals and the change ledger are not affected.
mcpServer.error.load: Failed to load MCP server status: {message}
mcpServer.network.desc: Expose the MCP server to the internet through a Cloudflare tunnel so clients that are not on this computer (for example a ChatGPT connector) can use it. The default is a temporary address; you can also configure your own domain for a fixed address. Only tokens created with “Allow use over the internet” can be used from the internet.
mcpServer.network.addressChanges: A Quick Tunnel address changes every time it is enabled; put the new address into your client after enabling.
mcpServer.network.needToken: First create a token with “Allow use over the internet” in the Clients tab, then network mode can be turned on.
mcpServer.network.confirm: This exposes the MCP server to the internet. Anyone holding a network token can call it (writes still need your approval in Magi). Enable it?
mcpServer.network.autoStop: The tunnel closes automatically when there is no valid network token, the server is stopped, or all tokens are revoked.
mcpServer.token.allowNetwork: Allow over the internet (permission cannot exceed “Edit”)
mcpServer.token.noSecret: Magi has no stored value for this token, so it cannot be shown. Choose Regenerate to get a new token (the old one stops working immediately).
mcpServer.token.rotateConfirm: After regenerating the token for "{client}", the old token stops working immediately and the client must be updated. Continue?
mcpServer.token.editWorkspaceFixed: Workspace: {workspace} (cannot be changed after creation; create a new token to use another workspace)
mcpServer.token.editNetworkDropped: Trusted edit and command execution cannot be exposed to the network, so network access for this token is turned off when you save.
mcpServer.token.editEffect: Takes effect from the client's next call. When access is narrowed, approvals this client is waiting on are cancelled.
mcpServer.snippets.perClientHint: The server name in this configuration is {name}, so it can sit next to other clients' configurations. The token is filled in — only put it in clients you trust.
mcpServer.snippets.placeholderOption: Don't fill in a token (keep the placeholder)
mcpServer.snippets.noSecretOption: no stored value, cannot be filled in
mcpServer.snippets.noSecretHint: Clients marked “no stored value” cannot have their token filled in. Use “Regenerate” in the Clients tab to get a new one.
mcpServer.snippets.placeholderNote: <MAGI_MCP_TOKEN> in the configuration is a placeholder: replace it with the token. In the stdio configuration MAGI_MCP_TOKEN is the environment variable name and its value is the token; in the HTTP configuration the token goes after Bearer in the Authorization header.
mcpServer.snippets.noTokens: There are no client tokens yet. A token identifies and authorizes one MCP client (for example Cursor or Claude Desktop) and must be created first.
mcpServer.snippets.stdioNote: The command in the stdio configuration is Magi's built-in mcp-relay; nothing else needs to be installed.
mcpServer.quickAdd.desc: The tunnel is ready. Pick a token that is allowed over the internet; the configuration below already contains the public address and the token. Only paste it into clients you trust.
mcpServer.quickAdd.form: Form fields (clients that ask for a server URL and a header)
mcpServer.quickAdd.json: JSON configuration (paste into the client's MCP config file)
mcpServer.quickAdd.fixedHint: This address is fixed; the configuration stays valid after Magi restarts.
mcpServer.direct.desc: If this computer has a public IP (or your router forwards a port to it), Magi can listen on a public address directly, without a tunnel. Listening on 0.0.0.0 means all network interfaces. Only tokens created with “Allow use over the internet” work from the internet; local-only tokens are never exposed.
mcpServer.direct.risk: Risk: this uses plain HTTP, so tokens travel unencrypted and anyone who can see the traffic can capture them. Use it only on trusted networks; for the internet, put a TLS-terminating reverse proxy (Nginx, Caddy, …) in front and expose only that.
mcpServer.direct.confirm: Anyone who can reach this port on this computer will be able to try the MCP server (a network token is required and writes still need your approval in Magi). Tokens are sent over plain HTTP. Turn it on?
mcpServer.direct.publicHosts: Public addresses clients use (domain or IP, one per line, no port)
mcpServer.direct.bindHint: 0.0.0.0 listens on all interfaces; you can also enter the IP of one interface. It must be an address of this computer.
mcpServer.direct.port: Port (leave empty to keep the current one)
mcpServer.direct.edit: Load current settings into the form
mcpServer.direct.firewall: Make sure your firewall / security group / router allows TCP port {port}, otherwise outside clients cannot connect.
mcpServer.direct.autoRestore: Once on, Magi restores the listener after a restart, and withdraws it when no valid internet-enabled token remains.
mcpServer.direct.restoreFailed: The previous public listener could not be restored and Magi fell back to local only: {message}
mcpServer.direct.plainHint: This address uses plain HTTP; use it only on trusted networks or put a TLS reverse proxy in front.
mcpServer.named.desc: Create a tunnel with your own Cloudflare account and domain to get a fixed public address. While network mode is on, Magi restores this tunnel after a restart, so client configuration never changes.
mcpServer.named.assist: New to Cloudflare? Type /magi-cloudflare-tunnel in the chat input and Magi will walk you through it in the built-in browser (you sign in and copy the token yourself).
mcpServer.named.modeNamed: Using a fixed address: {hostname}. It stays the same after Magi restarts.
mcpServer.named.tokenHidden: The tunnel token is stored on this computer and is never shown again.
mcpServer.named.autoRestore: While network mode is on, Magi restores this tunnel automatically after a restart.
mcpServer.named.tokenPlaceholder: Paste the token or the whole install command from the Cloudflare tunnel page
mcpServer.named.portHint: In the tunnel's “Public hostname” on Cloudflare, set the service to HTTP and the URL to 127.0.0.1:{port}.
mcpServer.named.clearConfirm: Network mode will be turned off and remote clients will be disconnected. You can turn on a temporary address afterwards. Continue?
mcpServer.named.verifyResult.ok: Connection works: Magi's MCP endpoint is reachable from the public internet.
mcpServer.named.verifyResult.not_configu: No named tunnel is configured yet.
mcpServer.named.verifyResult.network_off: Turn on network mode and wait for the tunnel to be ready, then check again.
mcpServer.named.verifyResult.dns_unresol: The domain does not resolve to Cloudflare yet: make sure the domain is on Cloudflare and the tunnel's public hostname is saved.
mcpServer.named.verifyResult.tunnel_not_: Cloudflare has no tunnel connection (status {status}): check the token and that network mode is on.
mcpServer.named.verifyResult.origin_unre: The tunnel is connected but forwarding failed (status {status}): check that the public hostname URL uses port {port}.
mcpServer.named.verifyResult.unexpected: Unexpected response (status {status}): check the public hostname settings.
mcpServer.network.error.tunnel_dependenc: cloudflared could not be downloaded or found. Check your network and try again.
mcpServer.network.error.tunnel_start_fai: The tunnel failed to start. Check the configuration and try again.
mcpServer.network.error.tunnel_connectio: The tunnel connection was lost. Turn network mode on again.
mcpServer.network.error.tunnel_token_inv: The tunnel token is invalid or revoked. Copy a new one from Cloudflare and replace it.
